licence_quote: 'Public Domain with Attribution'

name: NOAA NGS Emergency Response Imagery (ERI)
platform: crewed aircraft (NOAA King Air / Twin Otter)

what_we_could_show: Post-storm photo of each roof: tarps, missing shingles, fallen trees
notes: CAP and Maxar layers on NOAA viewers stay rejected

name: OpenAerialMap / Open Imagery Network
coverage: ad hoc; very sparse over US blocks
licence_quote: AWS registry: 'All imagery is publicly licensed CC-BY 4.0'. The per-image licence field must still be checked (some Maxar uploads are CC BY-NC)
what_we_could_show: Drone close-up of a roof where a volunteer flew it

name: USGS 3DEP LiDAR (EPT/COPC)
licence_quote: 'US Government Public Domain'
what_we_could_show: Every laser point on roofs and trees (core of the 3D blocks)

name: NGA/HSIP 133 US Cities LiDAR (USGS Non_Standard_Contributed)
measures: classified LAS point clouds (the AWS bucket also has orthos and footprints)
coverage: 133 metros incl. Austin, Birmingham, Cincinnati, Columbus OH, Dallas, Denver, Huntsville, Kansas City, Minneapolis, Phoenix, Houston, Seattle, Philadelphia, Chicago, Tulsa; usually two epochs each, ~2006-2012 (Austin 2006 + 2011, Denver 2007 + 2012, Minneapolis 2007 + 2012, KC 2009 + 2012)
access: https://rockyweb.usgs.gov/vdelivery/Datasets/Staged/Elevation/Non_Standard_Contributed/NGA_US_Cities/<City>/ (free HTTPS). The AWS copy s3://usgs-lidar-uscities is Requester Pays, so avoid it
cost: free via rockyweb (AWS copy bills the requester)
licence_quote: 'US Government Public Domain'
what_we_could_show: A 2nd/3rd LiDAR epoch per house: tree growth over the roof since 2006/2011, new extensions, removed trees, new pools. Draw all points and colour the deviations
notes: Each city folder has a readme PDF with caveats. Check the datum and vertical reference before differencing

name: NOAA Digital Coast Coastal LiDAR (incl. topobathy, JALBTCX)
coverage: US coasts + Great Lakes. Blocks with footprints: Fort Lauderdale, Houston, New Orleans, San Diego, Seattle, Levittown, Somerville, DC, Philadelphia, Orlando, Detroit, Oak Park, Honolulu
licence_quote: 'NOAA data disseminated through NODD are open to the public and can be used as desired.' 'NOAA requests attribution for the use or dissemination of unaltered NOAA data.'
what_we_could_show: Extra LiDAR epochs per roof and tree (e.g. 2001 HCFCD Harris Co, 2012 USACE New Orleans, 2017/2018 NGS topobathy Fort Lauderdale)
notes: Some DAV entries are partner data. The NODD licence covers the copies in the NOAA bucket; check partner terms for anything hosted elsewhere

name: NOAA NGS Coastal Mapping Program DSS/RCD30 orthos (Digital Coast imagery)
coverage: coastal cities: Philadelphia 2022 + 2026 (flown 10-12 May 2026), Boston 2017/2020/2022, Fort Lauderdale 2019, San Diego shore 2024-25, many more
access: bulk GeoTIFF https://coastalimagery.blob.core.windows.net/digitalcoast/<Name>_<id>/index.html ; metadata in InPort, e.g. https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/inport/item/80161
licence_quote: InPort: Access Constraints 'None'. Use Constraints are a disclaimer only ('Data set is not for use in litigation'). No explicit licence. It is a US federal work (17 U.S.C. 105), but the page does not say so
what_we_could_show: Fresh 2026 4-band ortho of the Philadelphia rows (roofs, trees, NDVI)
notes: GREY under the owner's rule (no explicit licence). A one-line statement from NGS/NODD would make it GREEN

name: OpenTopography hosted LiDAR (NCALM and others)
resolution: e.g. Austin TX15_Rapid 12.7 pts/m2, 0.5 m DEM
coverage: per project. Blocks hit: austin-tx (TX15_Rapid, June 2015), boulder-co (BcCZO 2010), portland-or (DOGAMI 2007-10), salt-lake-city-ut (UGS Wasatch 2013-14), san-diego-ca (SAN2005)
access: catalog API https://portal.opentopography.org/API/otCatalog?productFormat=PointCloud&minx=..&outputFormat=json ; bulk download links on each dataset page (no login). The global DEM API needs a free key
login_or_key: none for bulk; free key for API jobs
licence_quote: OT policy: 'Data obtained from OpenTopography are free of all copyright restrictions and made fully and freely available for both non-commercial and commercial uses.' Austin TX15_Rapid page: 'Use License: CC BY 4.0'
what_we_could_show: A dense 2015 post-flood LiDAR epoch for the Austin block (12.7 pts/m2, denser than 3DEP): roof planes, tree change
notes: The licence is per dataset, so record it per project (DOGAMI, UGS and BcCZO not yet checked). A citation is required

name: Missouri MSDIS statewide aerial imagery (2023 north, 2024 south)
coverage: Missouri. Jackson Co 2024, Clay Co 2024 and Platte Co 2023 cover the kansas-city-mo block
access: s3://mo-gis-imagery (us-west-2, public; ~220 MB tiles, read with HTTP range requests), e.g. Data/2024_SouthernMissouriImagery/2024_Jackson_Tiles/
licence_quote: 'Access to Missouri aerial imagery distributed by the Missouri Spatial Data Information Service (MSDIS) is governed by Creative Commons BY 4.0 (CC BY 4.0)'
what_we_could_show: 6-inch 2024 leaf-off roof view for the Kansas City block
already_in_app: no. imagery.md currently REJECTS MSDIS as 'terms not explicit'
notes: MSDIS manages the registry entry itself (bucket populated Oct 2026). The rejection should be reversed

name: Indiana IGIO statewide orthoimagery (leaf-off + 2025 leaf-on)
resolution: 3-6 inch leaf-off; leaf-on at NAIP class
licence_quote: 'Access to Indiana Geographic Information Office Orthoimagery is governed by Creative Commons 0 (CC0)'
what_we_could_show: Sub-foot roofs for any Indiana block added later

name: DC OCTO orthophotos 1995-2025 (+ 2026 snow) and LiDAR 2015/2018/2020/2022
resolution: ortho 0.08 m (3 inch, flown 27 Mar 2025); LiDAR city-wide
access: https://imagery.dcgis.dc.gov/dcgis/rest/services/Ortho/Ortho_2025/ImageServer (keyless); DCGIS_DATA/Ortho2026_SnowWebMercator; LiDAR as Open Data DC items (2022 Classified LAS da0c156ef3d24607b27a0da418970eac); s3://dc-lidar-2015 , s3://dc-lidar-2018
licence_quote: Open Data DC items 'Aerial Photography (Orthophoto) - 2025' and '2022 LiDAR - Classified LAS': licence CC-BY-4.0. dc.gov terms: DC Open Data 'is public domain and made available with a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal dedication'
what_we_could_show: 3-inch 2025 roofs, biennial history back to 1995, a 2026 snow-day image (snow that melts first suggests heat loss), four LiDAR epochs

name: New Jersey statewide imagery/LiDAR (NJOGIS on AWS)

what_we_could_show: Roof material class (asphalt vs tile vs metal) and methane-plume flags where a line crosses
notes: An Earthdata login means the user has to create an account
